question: Before applying for an Iowa real estate broker's license, an applicant must have been a licensed real estate salesperson actively engaged in real estate for at least how many months preceding the date of application (or have had substantially equivalent experience)?
explanation: Iowa Code section 543B.15(7) requires a broker applicant to have been a licensed real estate salesperson actively engaged in real estate for at least 24 months preceding the date of application, or to have had experience substantially equal to that which a licensed salesperson would ordinarily receive during a 24-month period (as a former broker, salesperson, real estate manager, or otherwise).

question: In addition to the required salesperson prelicense course, an applicant for an Iowa real estate broker's license must complete how many contact hours of commission-approved broker education, and within what time frame prior to taking the broker examination?
choice_a: 90 contact hours within 36 months prior to the broker examination
choice_b: 30 contact hours within 12 months prior to the broker examination
choice_c: 60 contact hours within 24 months prior to the broker examination
choice_d: 45 contact hours within 18 months prior to the broker examination
explanation: Iowa Code section 543B.15(7) states that to qualify for a broker's license, a person must complete at least 60 contact hours of commission-approved real estate education within 24 months prior to taking the broker examination, and this education is in addition to (not a substitute for) the required salesperson prelicense course.

question: Iowa's broker prelicense curriculum under IAC 481—2016.3(543B) is built from nine named subject courses. What is the total number of hours these nine courses must add up to?
explanation: IAC 481—2016.3(1) lists nine broker prelicense subjects (Contract Law and Contract Writing, Iowa Real Estate Trust Accounts, Principles of Appraising and Market Analysis, Real Estate Law and Agency Law, Real Estate Finance, Federal and State Laws Affecting Iowa Practice, Real Estate Office Organization/Administration/Human Resources, Real Estate Technology and Data Security, and Ethics and Safety Issues for Brokers) whose hours sum to the 60 total hours required by Iowa Code section 543B.15(7).

question: According to the Iowa Real Estate Commission's testing vendor (PSI), a broker exam candidate at the test center must present proof of course completion certificates for the broker prelicense curriculum. How many separate certificates does this typically require, given the structure of the commission-approved broker curriculum?
explanation: Because IAC 481—2016.3(1) organizes the 60-hour broker prelicense curriculum into nine distinct named courses (Contract Law and Contract Writing, Iowa Real Estate Trust Accounts, Principles of Appraising and Market Analysis, Real Estate Law and Agency Law, Real Estate Finance, Federal and State Laws Affecting Iowa Practice, Real Estate Office Organization/Administration/Human Resources, Real Estate Technology and Data Security, and Ethics and Safety Issues for Brokers), an approved provider typically issues one certificate per completed course — meaning a broker candidate presents nine separate completion certificates at the test center, versus a single prelicense certificate for salesperson candidates.
source_note: IAC 481—2016.3(1)(543B); PSI Candidate Handbook for Iowa Real Estate Examinations

question: An applicant for an Iowa real estate salesperson license must complete how many hours of commission-approved prelicense education, and within what period before taking the salesperson examination?
choice_a: 30 hours within 12 months prior to the examination
choice_b: 60 hours within 12 months prior to the examination
choice_c: 45 hours within 6 months prior to the examination
choice_d: 60 hours within 24 months prior to the examination
explanation: IAC 481—2004.1(7) and 481—2016.2(1) require the salesperson licensing examination's mandatory course of study to consist of 60 live instruction or online learning hours of real estate principles and practices, completed during the 12 months prior to taking the examination, to satisfy Iowa Code section 543B.15(8).

question: Iowa's 60-hour salesperson prelicense curriculum is divided into five subject modules of 12 hours each. Which of the following is one of those five required modules?
choice_a: Real Estate Technology and Data Security
choice_b: Real Estate Office Organization, Administration and Human Resources
choice_c: Ownership, Encumbrances, Legal Descriptions, Transfer of Title and Closing
choice_d: Ethics and Safety Issues for Brokers
explanation: IAC 481—2016.2(1)(a) lists the five 12-hour salesperson prelicense modules as: Introduction to Real Estate and Iowa License Law; Ownership, Encumbrances, Legal Descriptions, Transfer of Title and Closing; Contracts, Agency and Antitrust; Valuation, Finance and Real Estate Math; and Property Management/Leasing, Fair Housing, Environmental Risks and Health Issues. The other three answer choices are broker-level prelicense courses under IAC 481—2016.3(1), not part of the salesperson curriculum.

question: At the time an applicant submits an original Iowa salesperson license application, the applicant must also provide evidence of completing three additional live-instruction courses beyond the 60-hour prelicense curriculum. What are those three courses and how many hours does each require?
choice_a: 8 hours each of Law Update, Ethics, and Fair Housing
choice_b: 6 hours each of Contract Law, Agency Law, and Real Estate Finance
choice_c: 24 hours each of Electives, Ethics, and Law Update
choice_d: 12 hours each of Developing Professionalism and Ethical Practices, Buying Practices, and Listing Practices
explanation: IAC 481—2016.2(1)(b) requires that, at the time an application for an original salesperson license is submitted, the applicant also provide evidence of 12 hours of Developing Professionalism and Ethical Practices, 12 hours of Buying Practices, and 12 hours of Listing Practices — all completed during the 12 months prior to the date the application is postmarked or received. This is separate from, and in addition to, the 60-hour prelicense course of study required before sitting for the exam.

question: What is the current fee the Iowa Real Estate Commission charges for an original real estate broker's license?
explanation: IAC 481—2009.1(1) sets the fee for an original or renewal broker license at $170. (By comparison, the salesperson license fee is $125; $195 is the total broker renewal fee once the $25 late-renewal penalty is added, and $150 is the equivalent late salesperson renewal total.)

question: What is the current fee the Iowa Real Estate Commission charges for an original real estate salesperson's license?
explanation: IAC 481—2009.1(1) sets the fee for an original or renewal salesperson license at $125, compared to $170 for a broker license. The $50 figure is the fee for a branch office, trade name, or additional officer/partner license, and $95 corresponds to the separately administered examination fee paid to the testing vendor, not the license fee itself.

question: After passing the qualifying real estate examination, an Iowa broker or salesperson applicant must submit a completed license application, fee, and proof of education by what deadline?
choice_b: The last working day of the third calendar month following the exam
choice_c: The last working day of the sixth calendar month following the exam
choice_d: One year after passing the exam
explanation: IAC 481—2003.3(543B) (broker) and 481—2004.3(543B) (salesperson) both require the completed application, license fee, proof of required education, and test score report to be submitted to the commission no later than the last working day of the sixth calendar month following the qualifying real estate examination.

question: Iowa Code section 543B.15(9) requires a national criminal history check for initial broker and salesperson applicants. Within how many calendar days of the criminal history check's completion must the commission receive the completed license application, or else the application is rejected and returned?
explanation: Iowa Code section 543B.15(9) provides that unless the criminal history check was completed within the 210 calendar days prior to the date the license application is received by the commission, the commission must reject and return the application to the applicant. This 210-day window is echoed in both IAC 481—2003.3 (broker) and 481—2004.3 (salesperson).

question: Iowa real estate broker and salesperson licenses are issued for a fixed multiyear term. What is that term, and when does it expire?
choice_a: A three-year term expiring on December 31 of the third year
choice_b: A two-year term expiring on June 30 of the second year
choice_c: A one-year term expiring on the anniversary of issuance
choice_d: A five-year term expiring on December 31 of the fifth year
explanation: IAC 481—2003.3(2) (broker) and 481—2004.3(2) (salesperson) both provide that licenses are issued for a three-year term, with the remaining portion of the year of issuance counted as a full year, and that all licenses expire on December 31 of the third year of the license term.

question: A broker or salesperson who misses the December 31 renewal deadline is given a grace period to renew late. How long is that grace period, and what penalty applies?
choice_b: 30 days (until January 30), plus a $25 penalty added to the regular renewal fee
choice_d: There is no grace period; the license lapses immediately on January 1
explanation: Iowa Code section 543B.28 allows a licensee who fails to renew by the expiration date to do so within 30 days following expiration, subject to a reasonable penalty set by the commission. IAC 481—2003.5(2) and 481—2004.5(2) implement this by allowing renewal through midnight January 30 if accompanied by the regular renewal fee plus a $25 penalty (bringing the total to $195 for a broker or $150 for a salesperson).

question: A broker whose license expired and who missed the January 30 late-renewal deadline wants to reinstate it. Under IAC 481—2003.6(543B), within what window can the license still be reinstated, and what fee applies?
choice_a: Within 1 year, for a flat $100 fee
choice_b: Never — the applicant must start over as a salesperson immediately
choice_c: Within 3 years of expiration, for the regular renewal fee plus $25 for each partial or full month since expiration
choice_d: Within 5 years, for a flat $250 fee
explanation: IAC 481—2003.6(543B) (broker) and 481—2004.6(543B) (salesperson) allow reinstatement of an expired license within three years of expiration by submitting the regular renewal fee plus an additional reinstatement fee of $25 for each partial or full month following expiration. A licensee who fails to reinstate within three years is treated as if never licensed in Iowa and must start over in the licensing process (a former broker restarting at the salesperson level).

question: To renew an Iowa broker or salesperson license to active status, a licensee must complete 36 hours of approved continuing education. How are those 36 hours broken down by subject?
choice_a: 12 hours each of Developing Professionalism, Buying Practices, and Listing Practices
choice_b: 18 hours Law Update and 18 hours Ethics
choice_c: 36 hours of any elective course with no subject requirements
choice_d: 8 hours Law Update, 4 hours Ethics, and 24 hours Electives
explanation: IAC 481—2003.4(543B) (broker) and 481—2004.4(543B) (salesperson), together with 481—2016.4(543B), require a minimum of 36 hours of approved continuing education to renew to active status: 8 hours of Law Update, 4 hours of Ethics, and 24 hours of Electives. Licensees may carry forward up to 50 percent (capped at 18 hours) of excess hours to the next renewal period, but may never carry over hours toward the mandatory Law Update or Ethics requirements.

question: Under Iowa Code section 543B.21, what must a nonresident applicant file with the Iowa Real Estate Commission in order to be licensed as a broker or salesperson in Iowa?
choice_a: A certification from the state of original licensure confirming current licensure, no pending charges, and a record justifying Iowa licensure
choice_b: Nothing extra — nonresidents are automatically licensed upon paying the fee
choice_c: A certified copy of their home-state driver's license only
choice_d: Proof of Iowa residency obtained within the prior 12 months
explanation: Iowa Code section 543B.21 requires a nonresident applicant to comply with all requirements applicable to Iowa residents and to file a certification from the state of original licensure, signed by that state's duly authorized official, confirming the applicant is currently licensed there, that no charges are pending, and that the applicant's record there justifies issuing an Iowa license.

question: Does Iowa grant automatic real estate license reciprocity to every licensee from every other state?
choice_a: Yes, all out-of-state licensees are automatically issued an Iowa license upon request
choice_b: No — reciprocity exists only where the commission has entered a specific written reciprocal agreement with that state or jurisdiction
choice_c: No — Iowa has no reciprocity provision of any kind and requires every applicant to retake full prelicense education
choice_d: Yes, but only for brokers, never for salespersons
explanation: IAC 481—2005.4(543B) provides that the commission 'may,' as authorized by Iowa Code section 543B.21, enter into specific written reciprocal licensing agreements or memorandums with individual states or jurisdictions having similar licensing criteria, granting Iowa licenses to those states' licensees on the same basis Iowa licensees are treated there. Reciprocity is therefore agreement-specific and discretionary, not a blanket rule covering every state.

question: A broker licensed in a state that does NOT have a reciprocal licensing agreement with Iowa wants an Iowa broker license. Under IAC 481—2005.3(543B), what path is available?
choice_a: They are permanently barred from Iowa licensure
choice_b: They must wait five years before applying
choice_c: They may be issued a comparable Iowa license by passing the required Iowa real estate examination, provided they meet the broker criteria and their license has not lapsed more than six months
choice_d: They may only be licensed as a salesperson, never as a broker
explanation: IAC 481—2005.3(543B) allows a nonresident licensed as a broker or salesperson in a state without a reciprocal agreement with Iowa (or who does not otherwise qualify for reciprocity) to obtain a comparable Iowa license by passing the applicable examination, so long as the person meets the Iowa broker criteria under 481—2003.1(543B) and their out-of-state license has not been inactive or expired for more than six months immediately preceding passage of the exam.

question: Under Iowa Code section 543B.27(2), how is the license fee calculated for a nonresident applicant whose home state charges Iowa residents a higher nonresident fee than it charges its own residents?
choice_a: The nonresident is always charged double the standard Iowa fee
choice_b: The nonresident is exempt from all Iowa licensing fees
choice_c: The nonresident pays only the standard Iowa fee regardless of their home state's fee structure
choice_d: The nonresident is charged the greater of the standard Iowa fee or the fee that state would charge an Iowa resident applying there
explanation: Iowa Code section 543B.27(2) contains a retaliatory fee provision: a nonresident applicant is charged the greater of (a) the standard fee set under subsection 1, or (b) the fee that person's home state would charge an Iowa resident applying for a license there, if that state charges nonresidents more than it charges its own residents.

question: According to the PSI Candidate Handbook governing Iowa real estate licensing exams, what happens to a candidate's $95 examination fee and 90-day registration if the candidate does not test within the registration window?
choice_a: The $95 fee is nonrefundable, and the candidate's eligibility registration expires after 90 days, requiring a new registration and fee to test
choice_b: The fee is automatically refunded in full and the registration is extended indefinitely
choice_c: The fee converts into continuing education credit
choice_d: There is no registration expiration; candidates may test at any time after paying once
explanation: Per the PSI Candidate Handbook for Iowa real estate examinations (administered under the commission's testing contract authority in IAC 481—2009.3), the $95 examination fee for either the salesperson or broker exam is nonrefundable, and a candidate's registration eligibility period expires 90 days after issuance, after which the candidate must re-register and pay the fee again to test.
source_note: PSI Candidate Handbook for Iowa Real Estate Examinations; IAC 481—2009.3(543B) (examination fee set by commission-testing service contract)
